spec.name: El Badi Palace
spec.description: El Badi Palace is a monumental Saadian palace in the Kasbah of Marrakech. It was commissioned by Sultan Ahmad al-Mansur following the Saadian victory over Portugal at the Battle of the Three Kings in 1578. Designed as a symbol of royal power and wealth, the palace was built with luxurious materials including marble, carved stucco, cedar wood and imported decorative elements. Its vast central courtyard was organized around a large reflecting pool, gardens and richly decorated pavilions. After the decline of the Saadian dynasty, much of the palace was dismantled under the Alaouite sultan Moulay Ismail and its valuable materials were reused in other royal projects. Today, its monumental ruins preserve the scale and organization of one of the most ambitious palaces of Saadian Morocco.

timeline.title: Construction begins
timeline.description: Sultan Ahmad al-Mansur began the construction of El Badi Palace after the Saadian victory at the Battle of the Three Kings.

timeline.title: Major palace construction
timeline.description: By the end of the 16th century, El Badi had developed into an elaborate royal complex centered on a vast courtyard with pools, gardens and monumental pavilions.

timeline.title: Death of Ahmad al-Mansur
timeline.description: Ahmad al-Mansur died in 1603. The Saadian state subsequently entered a period of political division and decline.

timeline.title: Dismantling of the palace
timeline.description: During the reign of the Alaouite sultan Moulay Ismail, much of El Badi Palace was stripped of its valuable decorative materials, many of which were reused in other royal construction projects.
